In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism
2D.1 There is but one God, the LORD God the Father.
2E.2 God is faithful to those that love Him, and keeps His covenant and mercy with them (God acknowledges those who love Him).
3A.8 It is not good to do anything which causes your brother to stumble, or become offended, or be made weak.

precepts.text: Though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, to us there is but one God, the Father, and one Lord Jesus Christ. Because we understand there is only one living God, that is why the king was marveling.
precepts.point: The mother was marvelous above all and worthy of honorable memory: she saw her seven sons slain in one day, and bare it with good courage because of her hope in the Lord. The Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again. And what kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God, if he allows them to do that to us and then they get the same portion.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

note.label: CHRIST THE GOD THE REDEEMER

precepts.why:
“As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world”. An idol is nothing.

So when Isaiah 52:3 says “Ye have sold yourselves for nought”, it means we sold ourselves for idols. By worshipping idols and going after other gods we allowed ourselves to be sold, and the curses came upon us.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” That is Christ. “All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.” All things were made by Christ: the one Lord by whom are all things.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why:
“For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible.” The sun, moon, stars and planets, everything on earth, and things you cannot see with the naked eye: all created by Jesus Christ, our Father, our Messiah, our God. “Whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.”

That is why he is going to put everything under his feet: it belonged to him in the first place. And we, being heirs with Christ, he is going to give those things to us, if we are faithful and fervent. That is the only way we are going to get it.

“And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.” That is why he is the Alpha and Omega.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why:
“Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds.” When Christ was on the scene, that was considered the last days; the last days started then.

Christ made the worlds, meaning he made everything. He was before the beginning, and he made the beginning you read about in Genesis. He is the heir of all things, and he prefers the nation of Israel: the so-called blacks, Hispanics and natives, those of slave descent, of Israelite descent.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

precepts.why:
“Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth.” Plain and simple. Nothing changed in the New Testament. He created everybody, but he only knew Israel: he had that special relationship with Israel, he preferred Israel.

“Therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.” That is why the royal line of David was taken into captivity. The slave ships existed because of iniquity, and the prison system exists because of iniquity, because we are in sin. Now it is time to come up out of that sin.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”: there, in the lands where we are scattered, we would serve gods made by men, carved in wood and stone, or molten in silver and gold. Back then those were the idols of old; in modern times it would be Christianity and Islam. Make-believe gods, action figures called gods: Ken and Barbie called gods, Ninja Turtles, Transformers, Power Rangers called gods. Made by men’s hands, “which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell”, because they’re not alive. They’re toys. Nothing in the world.

The there is in verse 27: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen.” Who is Paul writing to in Corinthians? Israelites. Corinth is in Greece. Israel is scattered among all nations and all lands, Greece, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Iraq, Iran, India, Hawaii, Fiji, Madagascar, so Paul is writing to Israelites living in a foreign land. That is us being scattered, what Moses was talking about.

So when Paul says an idol is nothing in the world, he is saying what the law already said.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why: “And have cast their gods into the fire: for they were no gods.” How do you cast a god into a fire? Because there isn’t a god. They were nothing in the world, “but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone: therefore they have destroyed them.” They are destroyable because they are toys. Put a toy in the microwave on the highest heat and it’ll melt. It is not a god.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“He is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” All the gods of the nations are idols; our God made the heavens.

That is what Paul said: we know, we have the knowledge, that there is but one God, one true God, with the Son.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.” The nations’ idols are sculpted to have mouths, like an action figure has a mouth, “but they speak not”. Eyes they are given, “but they see not”: that is what Moses said. Ears, but they hear not; noses, but they smell not. Hands, “but they handle not”: they can’t hold anything. Feet, “but they walk not.”

“They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.” They that make them are just like them, dead objects, and so are you that believe these things are real gods: dead like your toy, dumb like your toy, fake like your toy. That is what David said.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why: David says it again: “The idols of the heathen are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; eyes have they, but they see not; They have ears, but they hear not; neither is there any breath in their mouths.” They’re not alive. “They that make them are like unto them: so is every one that trusteth in them.” David said it twice: nothing in the world.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
See what David’s son says about idols. “But miserable are they, and in dead things is their hope, who call them gods, which are the works of men’s hands”: the nations. “Gold and silver, to shew art in”: the art is the eyes, the ears, the nose, the mouth, the colour, the paints. “And resemblances of beasts”: an idol made like an animal, like a goat.

“Or a stone good for nothing”: you kiss it and it does nothing for you. “The work of an ancient hand”: it has been around since ancient idolatry.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it”: the idol is cursed, and he that made it is cursed, “because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.” Corruptible because it can be destroyed: it grows old, it rusts, it rots, and it was called a god.

“For the ungodly and his ungodliness are both alike hateful unto God”, and “that which is made shall be punished together with him that made it”: not only is the idol destroyed, the person that made it is destroyed along with it.

“Therefore even upon the idols of the Gentiles shall there be a visitation”, because they are “stumblingblocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the unwise.” Esau is going to pay for that, and Ishmael is going to pay for Islam too.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“Both they that make them, they that desire them, and they that worship them, are lovers of evil things”: we saw that at the 2819 church. They “are worthy to have such things to trust upon”: they are evil as hell, and they are going to die.

The potter, “tempering soft earth”, fashions vessels “for our service”: he makes pots and bowls and sells them to the people. Some “serve for clean uses”, a bowl, a vase to hold flowers, and some do the contrary. But “employing his labours lewdly”, wickedly, “he maketh a vain god of the same clay”, the same soft clay used to make bowls and cups, “even he which a little before was made of earth himself.” A man making a god makes no sense. How can a man, a mortal being, make an eternal being? It’s ridiculous.

He returns to the earth “when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.” Your body doesn’t belong to you: your life was lent you. This is a rental, and the same way you got it, you have to return it. That means not getting high, not getting drunk, not defiling your body. It belongs to him, and it shall be demanded.

The idol maker “striveth to excel goldsmiths and silversmiths” and “counteth it his glory to make counterfeit things”: going out of his way to prove he is better than a goldsmith or a silversmith by making fake gods. “His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile than earth, and his life of less value than clay”: the lives of those who make idols are worthless, “Forasmuch as he knew not his Maker”. He doesn’t care about the God that made him; he cares about making gods.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
“And all the enemies of thy people, that hold them in subjection, are most foolish”: the heathen that have us in captivity are stupid, “more miserable than very babes”, because they are not God’s people. They have no God, no guidance; they are not chosen at all. They are here to make our lives hell for breaking God’s laws; outside of that they have no purpose. By default, every nation outside of the nation of Israel, their god is the devil. Satan plays with your imagination, and the nations make gods according to their imagination: heathen gods are figments of heathen imagination. And Israelites have adopted those gods into our lives.

“For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle”: the same thing his father David said.

“For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them”: your spirit was lent to you; it is a loan. “But no man can make a god like unto himself”: no man can make a god that can see, hear, eat, think and walk. So idols are nothing in the world.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

precepts.why:
An example of meat in the idol’s temple. “Now the Babylons had an idol, called Bel”: as Paul said, there be that are called gods, gods many and lords many. Beelzebub means lord of the flies; Baal-peor; Bel means lord. It all goes back to lords: gods are lords.

“There were spent upon him every day twelve great measures of fine flour, and forty sheep, and six vessels of wine”, huge vessels, all to reverence this idol. “And the king worshipped it and went daily to adore it: but Daniel worshipped his own God.”

Asked why he did not worship Bel, Daniel answered, “Because I may not worship idols made with hands, but the living God, who hath created the heaven and the earth, and hath sovereignty over all flesh.” That is what David said, what Moses said, and what Solomon said.

PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: To us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things: the grandfather and the father, clear and concise.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

points: “But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.” By whom are all things: principalities, everything you see on the earth and in the heavens, the sun, the moon and the stars. Christ created everything, even us. “And we by him”, because Christ our Father created us.
He created everything, but he prefers Israel.

note.label: Sons of Jacob: A Shadow of Things to Come

points: This is where all the confusion about Paul lies. “Now as touching things offered unto idols”: that is the context, things offered to idols. “We know that we all have knowledge”: concerning idols, they all knew they had knowledge. Keep that in mind; Paul goes on to explain what that knowledge is.

When you read Paul’s letters, the understanding comes either above the verse, within the verse or under the verse. If it is not found in those three places, he will often address the same situation in a different church, in a different letter, with more clarity, because the same situations tended to occur in multiple churches, and you cross reference them together.

“Knowledge puffeth up”: knowledge can puff you up and make you arrogant. “But charity edifieth”: whatever knowledge you may have, charity is the most important thing. Charity translates to love your neighbour as yourself. Charity is love.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “He knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know”: you know enough, but you don’t know everything. Don’t get arrogant. Don’t be puffed up.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “If any man love God, the same is known of him”: you will be known whether you love God by your actions.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols”: the context has not changed from verse 1. Paul is addressing eating things offered to idols.

“We know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.” The root of the word knowledge is to know. The knowledge the believers in Christ had in verse 1 is this: idols are nothing in the world. Idols are not gods; there is no God but one. Be mindful of what you know, and don’t get an ego from what you learn.

Paul was born and raised in the perfect manner of the law; he was not a fool. When he wrote letters, his source material was the law and the prophets. So whatever he says in this letter, we can go back into the law and find it there.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “For though there be that are called gods”: Zeus is called a god. Odin, Thor and Loki are called gods. Vishnu, Krishna and Allah are called gods. White Jesus is called a god. Bacchus, Mars, Mercury, Ares, Ashtoreth and Baal are called gods. “Whether in heaven”: some are known to dwell in heaven, paradise, Nirvana or Olympus; “or in earth”: some on earth, or under the water like Poseidon.
“As there be gods many, and lords many”: the Hindus have 37,000 gods, and yoga calls upon those gods. Don’t do yoga. Its positions are bowing down to them, which the law says not to do.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “But to us there is but one God”: to us, the Israelites. We are monotheistic; the other nations are polytheistic and worship many gods. “The Father, of whom are all things”: he is the architect. “And one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him”: his Son, whom he used to make everything, the master builder. Christ made us, and the Son was made by the Father. Grandfather, father: not the same entity. My dad is not my grandfather; my dad’s dad is my grandfather.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “Howbeit there is not in every man that knowledge”: the knowledge of verse 4, that idols are nothing in the world. “For some with conscience of the idol unto this hour eat it as a thing offered unto an idol”: some, stronger in the faith, understood that idols are nothing; others ate meat offered to idols and really believed in their own mind they were honouring that god. “And their conscience being weak is defiled”: defiled in believing that these idols are actually real gods.
Some of our people scattered among the nations were former idolaters, and others were raised heavily in Judaism to abhor and abstain from all idols at any cost. That was the dilemma here.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “But meat commendeth us not to God”: to be commended is to gain acknowledgement, to be accepted, like being commendable for your service around the house or at your job. Paul explains it within the verse: “for neither, if we eat, are we the better; neither, if we eat not, are we the worse.” Eating meat sacrificed to idols, or not eating it, does not bring you closer to God or further from him, because idols are nothing in the world.

If I set a Ninja Turtle toy by my plate and pray, oh heavenly Donatello, heavenly Leonardo, thank you for this chicken, does the food become defiled? No. I’m an idiot eating food. Heavenly Power Ranger, heavenly Zordon, heavenly Thundercats: the meat remains the meat. But some will say, you prayed to Ninja Turtles, that food is bad. That is the weak conscience. A lot of people really believe that doing that makes the food bad.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “But take heed lest by any means this liberty of yours become a stumblingblock to them that are weak.” The liberty is the knowledge that idols are nothing in the world, action figures. Be mindful, because not all your brothers are as strong as you. If I eat food offered to a toy action figure and a brother with a weak conscience, from an idolatrous background, sees me, he may think I’m an idolater, or that maybe it’s okay to worship the turtle. If that offends your brother, don’t eat it, because it will make him fall.

If you don’t know, you just don’t know: liberty means, once again, the knowledge that idols are nothing in the world. And you that know it are to be mindful of a brother or sister who is weak in the faith. Christians don’t understand that part, and it is the foolery they attack the prophets with today. Take good notes; if this is fluent to you, it will not be a problem.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “For if any man see thee which hast knowledge sit at meat in the idol’s temple”: in the Greco-Roman world Paul was writing to, in Corinth in Greece, temples were hubs for more than worship. Our own temple was multipurpose: sacrificing, feast days and worship, and business transactions too, until Christ got mad and threw the tables over. The heathen temples were also multipurpose: banquet halls, like the restaurants of today or the halls we rent for our feast days with a catering service, and community and business gathering spaces, rented out.

After an animal was sacrificed to an idol, a portion of the meat was burned, a portion given to the priest, and the rest eaten in a meal on the temple grounds or sold in the public market. It was the same with Levi in our temple: the meat was burned, eaten by the priests and by those who offered it, and the rest put in the storehouse. Some believers in Corinth with a strong conscience went to those meals and ate, knowing the idols were not real and the meat was just food. They went there for the food.

But the brother who comes from an idolatrous background sees you sitting there, and his conscience is “emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols”: he is convinced it’s okay to worship and reverence idols. That was a real point of disagreement and a stumbling block for those with a weak conscience, who felt it was a compromise with idolatry. Paul is saying, I get it, you know the idols around here are nothing, but you are offending other believers who are weaker, and leading people to believe we partake in idolatry. If it is going to cause your brother to fall, don’t eat there.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died?” You will either make him go back to idols or make him denounce the faith, because he sees you eating food offered to idols.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “But when ye sin so against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ”: you sin against Christ for being a bad example to your brother. As verse 1 said, knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth. Look out for your brother.

note.label: PAUL THE PROPHET AND IDOL WORSHIP

points: “Wherefore, if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth”: if eating there makes my brother offend, I will not eat that food.
